extra.message: The user-supplied GraphQL 'filter' argument is interpolated directly into a raw SQL fragment via Python '%' string formatting inside sqlalchemy.text(): text("title = '%s' or content = '%s'" % (filter, filter)). An attacker can supply filter="' or 1=1--" to bypass the WHERE clause and dump all pastes, or craft UNION/stacked queries.

ImportPaste builds a URL from the attacker-controlled host/port/path/scheme arguments (line 210) and passes it to helpers.run_cmd(), which calls os.popen(). In the default easy mode strip_dangerous_characters() is a no-op, so shell metacharacters such as ';', '|', backticks or $() allow arbitrary OS command execution (e.g. path="/ || id").

ImportPaste fetches an arbitrary URL assembled from client-controlled host/port/path/scheme via curl. There is no allow-list or SSRF protection, so an attacker can reach internal-only services (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:6379, http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) and exfiltrate the response, or use file:// to read local files.

The systemDiagnostics resolver passes the user-supplied 'cmd' GraphQL argument straight to helpers.run_cmd(cmd) (os.popen). In easy mode security.allowed_cmds() returns True for every value, so any authenticated client can execute arbitrary OS commands.

The systemDebug resolver concatenates the user-supplied 'arg' parameter into a shell command with 'ps {}'.format(arg) and executes it via helpers.run_cmd()/os.popen. No sanitization or allow-list is applied, enabling arbitrary command execution (e.g. arg="-ef; id").

save_file() concatenates the user-supplied 'filename' from the uploadPaste mutation directly onto WEB_UPLOADDIR and opens it for writing, with no normalization or traversal check. A filename such as '../../../../etc/cron.d/payload' writes attacker-controlled content to arbitrary filesystem paths, potentially achieving remote code execution.

get_identity() decodes the user-supplied JWT with options {"verify_signature": False, "verify_exp": False}. An attacker can forge an unsigned/attacker-signed token with identity='admin' and no valid expiry, completely bypassing authentication for the 'me' resolver and the admin password disclosure.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: run_cmd() executes its argument through os.popen(), a shell interpreter. Every caller that forwards untrusted input (systemDiagnostics, systemDebug, importPaste) therefore inherits arbitrary OS command execution. The function provides no escaping or argument separation.

Flask SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET_KEY are hardcoded to the literal 'dvga'. The random value assigned on line 10 (os.urandom(24)) is overwritten, so signed cookies/sessions use a publicly known key. Because the JWT secret is also known, tokens can be forged even if signature verification were enabled.

extra.message: Paste data received over the WebSocket subscription (paste.title, paste.content, paste.owner.name, paste.ipAddr, paste.userAgent) is interpolated raw into a JavaScript template literal and inserted into the DOM with jQuery prependTo. A paste containing <script> or an onerror handler executes in the browser of every subscriber, a stored XSS.

get_pastes() interpolates the attacker-controlled title, content, owner name, ipAddr and userAgent fields returned by the pastes query directly into HTML template literals and appends them to the galleries. Unsanitized paste content is therefore executed as HTML/JavaScript in any viewer's browser (stored XSS).

format_custom_error injects full Python stack traces (traceback.format_stack), the complete exception text (traceback.format_exc) and the server-side caller filename into GraphQL error responses under extensions.exception. Any client of /graphiql receives internal paths, source structure and debug details.

extra.message: The 'operator' account is seeded with the hardcoded plaintext password 'password123'. The credential is committed to source control and present in every deployment, allowing trivial authentication as that user.

random_password() selects from a single hardcoded value, ['changeme'], so the privileged 'admin' account always gets the password 'changeme'. This is a trivially guessable credential present in the source code.

The 'env' cookie that gates access to /graphiql is set with resp.set_cookie() without HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite attributes, and its value is trusted verbatim by IGQLProtectionMiddleware. A client can simply set env=graphiql:enable to enable the playground in hardened mode.

extra.message: simulate_load() runs a loop that sleeps 0.1s up to 500 times per invocation and is reachable through the unauthenticated systemUpdate query. With no rate limiting, concurrent requests tie up worker/CPU resources and cause a denial of service.

extra.message: sys.setrecursionlimit(100000) removes Python's normal recursion guard while the schema permits deeply nested/circular queries (e.g. pastes{owner{pastes{owner{...}}}}). An attacker can submit a deeply recursive query to exhaust the stack and crash the server.

The hardened-mode command allow-list contains adjacent string-literal concatenation: ('echo', 'ps' 'whoami', 'tail') evaluates to ('echo', 'pswhoami', 'tail'). The intended 'ps' and 'whoami' entries are never matched, and prefix-based startswith() allows 'echo'/'tail' with arbitrary arguments, defeating the allow-list.
